approval.approval_reference: Internal editorial checkpoint by GPT-5.6 Sol on 2026-08-13 after complete SP-2026-M01 Evidence normalization. All 13 CANDIDATE rows assigned editorial roles and clustered into a 32-page single-volume Architecture proposal. This reference is explicitly not Human Gate 1 approval.

FEATURE_CORE.title: OpenAI January agent-system engineering: Codex loop and in-house data agent
FEATURE_CORE.selection_rationale: The strongest January architecture anchor: the Codex agent loop and in-house data agent expose harness logic, layered context, memory, tool orchestration, and access-control boundaries beyond the base model.
remaining_boundaries: The two sources describe different systems and should remain separately attributed even when used as one architecture cluster.
The in-house data-agent lessons are organizational case-study evidence and should not be generalized as a universal architecture benchmark.

SECTION_CORE.title: Claude Cowork research preview and new Claude constitution
SECTION_CORE.selection_rationale: Cowork provides a clear desktop-agent execution surface while the new Claude constitution makes the behavioral-control layer explicit in the same month.
remaining_boundaries: Cowork was a research preview, so announcement-time product boundaries must not be generalized to later availability.
The constitution describes intended behavior and training guidance; actual model outputs may not always follow its ideals, as Anthropic itself notes.

SECTION_CORE.title: DynaWeb: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning of Web Agents
SECTION_CORE.selection_rationale: DynaWeb is a concrete training response to the cost, instability, and risk of allowing web agents to learn directly on the live web.
remaining_boundaries: A simulated web world model can differ materially from adversarial, dynamic live-web behavior.
The task locator is arXiv v2 updated after January; chronology should use the original January submission.

SECTION_CORE.title: Gemini API January 2026 tool and lifecycle updates
SECTION_CORE.selection_rationale: Gemini API Computer Use and external-input expansion are direct API-level evidence that frontier models were being connected to action tools and larger external context.
remaining_boundaries: Computer Use support is tied to preview model identifiers and must preserve announcement-time preview/deprecation status.
The changelog establishes API availability, not independent quality or safety of computer-use behavior.

SECTION_CORE.title: GLM-4.7-Flash and GLM-Image
SECTION_CORE.selection_rationale: GLM-4.7-Flash and GLM-Image provide a lightweight/open-model and multimodal counterpoint, with same-month downstream runtime integration.
remaining_boundaries: The task groups two distinct model releases because both establish the January Z.ai model line; drafting should not imply a single architecture.
Performance claims are vendor-reported and not independently reproduced.

SECTION_CORE.title: Mistral Vibe 2.0
SECTION_CORE.selection_rationale: Vibe 2.0 shows terminal-native coding agents evolving toward configurable subagents, skills, clarification loops, and explicit user-control mechanisms.
remaining_boundaries: The announcement is vendor-authored; claims about productivity or model quality are not independently reproduced.
Devstral 2 itself predates January, so the month-level event is the Vibe 2.0 agent/harness update rather than a new underlying model family.

SECTION_CORE.title: Qwen3-Max January Model Studio updates
SECTION_CORE.selection_rationale: Qwen3-Max January updates provide the model/API side of tool-native reasoning, including built-in retrieval, extraction, and code-interpreter use during thinking.
remaining_boundaries: Model Studio availability dates can differ by region and need to remain scoped to the listed deployment region.
The lifecycle page is living documentation; dated entries rather than current default aliases anchor January chronology.

SECTION_CORE.title: Safe URL / agent link data-exfiltration safeguards
SECTION_CORE.selection_rationale: OpenAI's safe-URL engineering note is direct production evidence that greater browsing/action autonomy creates a concrete data-exfiltration control problem.
remaining_boundaries: The mechanism targets URL-based exfiltration and does not establish that arbitrary web content is safe or that prompt injection is solved generally.
Security properties are implementation claims from OpenAI and are not independently penetration-tested here.

SECTION_CORE.title: SYNTHAGENT: synthetic tasks, simulated tools, rubric rewards
SECTION_CORE.selection_rationale: SYNTHAGENT complements DynaWeb with synthetic tasks, simulated tools, user simulation, and rubric rewards for training smaller tool-using agents.
remaining_boundaries: Synthetic environments provide stability but may underrepresent failures and adversarial conditions of real APIs.
The task locator is v2 updated after January; chronology should use the original submission date.

SECTION_CORE.title: Transformers v5 and v5.0.0rc3
SECTION_CORE.selection_rationale: Transformers v5 is a major common-tooling transition and compact evidence that the open ecosystem was standardizing fast-changing model families, loading, tokenization, and quantization paths.
remaining_boundaries: The RC and stable release occurred on the same date; stable v5 is the primary event and rc3 is supporting model-integration evidence.
Library support indicates implementation compatibility, not endorsement or independently measured model quality.

SECTION_CORE.title: vLLM v0.14.0 and v0.15.0
SECTION_CORE.selection_rationale: vLLM v0.14.0/v0.15.0 provides the strongest high-throughput serving/runtime anchor, including async scheduling, tool/API changes, and rapid new-model absorption.
remaining_boundaries: The series spans two releases nine days apart and should be summarized as serving/runtime evolution rather than one atomic feature.
Project performance claims are not independently reproduced.

SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.title: Prompt Injection Attacks on Agentic Coding Assistants
SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.selection_rationale: The prompt-injection systematization provides independent research context for the security boundary across coding assistants, tools, skills, and protocol ecosystems.
remaining_boundaries: This is a literature synthesis; its aggregate percentages depend on heterogeneous studies and should not be narrated as a single reproducible experiment.
The retained source is arXiv v1 from January; later research may revise the landscape.

SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.title: SGLang v0.5.8
SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.selection_rationale: SGLang v0.5.8 independently confirms rapid January runtime uptake across new model families, diffusion serving, long-context execution, and inference mechanisms.
remaining_boundaries: The release aggregates many upstream PRs and performance claims across different models/hardware.
Model support establishes implementation availability, not equivalent quality or production validation.

rules: Issue Architecture may group several selected items into one comparison package.
Supporting evidence is not a duplicate story and need not receive its own article package.
Do not add HOLD_OUT or EXCLUDE items without a new Selection revision bound to an updated matrix.
No section quota is required; weak sections may be omitted.
Article drafting begins only after the Architecture Plan validates successfully.
